facts.raw_span: A man in his 80s presented to the emergency department after 1 hour of chest pain and vomiting
The patient denied any history of hypertension and diabetes
Temperature: 36°C
Heart rate: 79 beats per minute
Blood pressure: 92/56 mm Hg
The maximal cardiac impulse was noted to be in the right fifth interspace
Hepatic dullness located in the left subcostal region
Initial serum troponin I level: 0.070 ng/mL
Initial ECG showed: Negative P waves in lead I
ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
